items.title: Chick Corea — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: One of the first bands I put together that I was real excited about was the band that finally made my first recording, Tones For Joan’s Bones, with Steve Swallow, Joe Farrell, Joe Chambers, and Woody Shaw.

ctx.x: Was that gig with Mongo how you became assimilated into the New York scene, and how people...

Well, it was one of the ways. The other way was through jam sessions and meeting people. I just had my ears and eyes open for any musical contact. Joe Farrell became an early kind of mentor for me. One of the first musicians I met when I got to New York who was my age, my friend Pete Yellin, the saxophone player. We used to hang out, playing and copying Charlie Parker solos. So he showed me around town. He was a New Yorker.
Where were you living when you got to New York?
